Setting up an app took four permission blocks, a topic-by-topic scatter of platform corners, and two hand-written lines in your `AndroidManifest.xml`. It takes four lines now, and your manifest needs nothing.

```kotlin
plugins {
    id("io.github.yuroyami.kiteconfig") version "2.0.0"
}

kiteConfig {
    appName = "Jetzy"
    appId   = "com.example.jetzy"
    version = "1.4.0"
    autoApply = true
}
```

## Requirements
- Gradle **8.5**+
- JDK **17** or **21**
- AGP **8.5.2** through **9.3.x**, KGP **2.4.x**, Compose **1.11** through **1.12.x**
- Old 1.0.0 names do not compile. The upgrade table is at the bottom.

## Changed
`autoApply = true` is the only switch for changing files you commit. It replaces every `rewrite { }` block, the `auto` flag inside each one, and the task names that went with them. With it off, nothing touches your sources until you run `./gradlew kiteApply`. `kiteApplyAndroid` and `kiteApplyIos` apply one platform, so an Android build can never drag iOS source edits along.

Platform differences live in that platform's own block, and the shared value sits at the root. Nothing is copied when a block opens, so a shared value written after a platform block still loses to it: declaration order decides nothing.

```kotlin
kiteConfig {
    appName = "Jetzy"
    appId   = "com.example.jetzy"
    android { appId { suffix = ".android" } }
    ios     { appName = "Jetzy Lite" }   // stop one value reaching one platform
}                                        // with ios { appName { enabled = false } }
```

A feature is on when you gave it what it needs. Set `logo { foreground }` and the icons install. A feature that needs nothing from you, like the launch screen, asks for `enabled = true`, so an empty `splash { }` no longer turns anything on.

Your Android manifest needs no KiteConfig lines. `android:label="${appName}"` and `android:theme="${kiteSplashTheme}"` are gone: KiteConfig writes its own manifest and lets AGP merge it over yours. The old lines still resolve if you keep them, and `kiteDoctor` now points out a manifest value of your own that the merge replaces.

Build numbers are text, so a dotted build number finally works on Apple. `VersionSchemes.DEFAULT` produces exactly the digits it always did, so an app already on a store keeps its numbering.

Blocks stay in their own scope. `android { skip(ios) }` used to call the root's skip and exclude iOS everywhere. It no longer compiles, and neither does `ios { jvm { } }`.

## Fixed
Fixed iOS ignoring the languages you list. `locales` reached iOS as `knownRegions` in the Xcode project, which never leaves that file, and a Compose app has no `.lproj` directories either, so iOS offered nothing. The tags now go into `Info.plist` as `CFBundleLocalizations`, which is what iOS actually reads.

Fixed the Android splash failing every AGP 9 build. Its generated resources went through the old source-set API, which AGP 9 refuses for generated output, so any project with the splash on could not configure at all.

Fixed an excluded platform still being read. Every gate resolved both sides before deciding, so `skip(desktop)` still queried the desktop block, and a provider that threw took down a build that had already excluded it.

Fixed a quoted brace or semicolon in the Xcode project being read as syntax. An app named `}` wrote a project file the next run refused to parse.

Fixed the iOS splash installing outside the ownership machinery, the JVM level reaching only Kotlin and not Java, and `kiteCheck` passing what an ordinary build refuses.

## Removed
`ios { deploymentTarget }` is gone. KiteConfig reads `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` from your Xcode project instead of asking you to restate it.

The generator and diagnostic task types are internal now. If you referenced one, address the task by name: `tasks.named("kiteInternalBuildConfig")`.

## Upgrading

| 1.0.0 | 2.0.0 |
| --- | --- |
| `id = "x"` | `appId = "x"` |
| `id("x") { android { suffix = ".a" } }` | `android { appId { suffix = ".a" } }` |
| `appName("x") { ios("y") }` | `ios { appName = "y" }` |
| `version("x") { formula { } }` | `version { scheme { } }` |
| `version("x") { android { reupload = 1 } }` | `android { version { rebuild = 1 } }` |
| `android { pin = 123 }` | `android { version { buildNumber = "123" } }` |
| `android { shipped = 1001003090 }` | `android { version { publishedBuildNumber = "1001003090" } }` |
| `ios { marketingVersion = "1.4" }` | `ios { version = "1.4" }` |
| `locales { pin("en") }` | `locales { tags = listOf("en") }` |
| `locales { filterAndroidRes = true }` | `android { locales { filterResources = true } }` |
| `logo { background = file(...) }` | `logo { background = image(file(...)) }` |
| `logo { backgroundColor = "#..." }` | `logo { background = color("#...") }` |
| `logo { android { safeZone = 0.6 } }` | `android { logo { foregroundScale = 0.6 } }` |
| `logo { desktop { roundMac = true } }` | `desktop { logo { roundMac = true } }` |
| `splash { }` turned it on | `splash { enabled = true }` |
| `jvmTarget = 21` | `jvm { target = 21 }` |
| `<topic> { skip(ios) }` | `ios { <topic> { enabled = false } }` |
| every `rewrite { }` block | `autoApply = true`, or run `kiteApply` |
| `ios { rewrite { targets("iosApp") } }` | `ios { xcodeTargets("iosApp") }` |
| `ios { rewrite { proMotion = true } }` | `ios { infoPlist { proMotion = true } }` |
| `ios { deploymentTarget = "15.0" }` | nothing: read from your Xcode project |
| `android:label="${appName}"` in your manifest | nothing: delete the line |
| `android:theme="${kiteSplashTheme}"` in your manifest | nothing: delete the line |
| `./gradlew kiteRewriteLogo`, `kiteRewriteXcode` | `./gradlew kiteApply` |
| `kiteConfig.id` | `kiteConfig.appId` |

`VersionCodeScheme.compute` returns `String` instead of `Int`. A scheme that returns an integer needs `.toString()`. `only()` with no arguments used to mean "everywhere"; it is now an error.

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/yuroyami/KiteConfig/compare/v1.0.0...v2.0.0
